title: Knocked-Out Tooth
summary: Hold the tooth by the crown, not the root. Put it back in its socket if you can; otherwise keep it moist in milk or saline and get to a dentist fast.

callEmergency.headline: Get to a dentist or emergency department as soon as possible
when: An adult tooth has been knocked out – the best chance of saving it is within the first hour
Mouth bleeding that won't stop, or a possible jaw fracture

steps.title: Find the tooth
steps.text: Pick it up by the crown (the white part). Do not touch the root.

steps.title: Rinse briefly if dirty
steps.text: Rinse for a few seconds in milk, saline or clean water. Do not scrub it.

steps.title: Put it back if you can
steps.text: If the person is alert and you are trained or confident, push the tooth gently back into its socket and have them bite on a clean cloth to hold it.

steps.title: If you cannot put it back
steps.text: Store it in milk or saline, or wrap it in cling film. Keep it with the person.

steps.title: Control bleeding
steps.text: Press a folded gauze pad on the socket and ask them to bite gently.

warningSigns: Jaw pain or difficulty opening the mouth
doNot: Do not hold the tooth by the root
Do not scrub the tooth or let it dry out
Do not store it in plain water for long
